extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of GAP (computational algebra system), including package authors and maintainers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for using the GAP system (help system, viewers, pager, command-line options) and for developing, documenting, distributing, and reporting issues for GAP packages and modifications to GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual as authoritative reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The GAP Reference Manual contains the official definitions of GAP functions and should contain all the information needed to use GAP; it is not intended to be read cover-to-cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the manual as the canonical source for function definitions; new users are advised to consult the GAP Tutorial for getting started. The manual is available as online help, PDF, and HTML; each package also ships with its own manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package contents and documentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A GAP package is a self-contained extension that contains GAP code and its own documentation, and may also include data files or external programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packages should provide documentation (a package manual) and may supply data or interfaces to external programs. Packages may be loaded via LoadPackage; some packages are loaded automatically if present. Note that packages depending on external programs may only be available on operating systems where those programs exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package refereeing and acceptance practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributed packages are subject to a refereeing system to ensure quality and to recognise authors; not all included packages have necessarily been refereed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packages that have passed refereeing are accepted in the same way as other accepted modules; some distributed packages may not (yet) have gone through refereeing and authors may choose not to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: License and redistribution terms (GAP core)
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP is distributed under the GNU General Public License (GPL) version 2 or (at your option) any later version; GAP is free software and may be redistributed or modified under the GPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may modify and redistribute GAP but you may not impose further restrictions that prevent redistribution (i.e., proprietary restrictions are forbidden). For full terms see the LICENSE file or https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl.html. Windows-distributed components (Cygwin parts) carry their respective licenses; GAP for Windows executables are distributed under the GPL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to supply README when redistributing modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If you modify any part of GAP and redistribute it, you must supply a README describing what modifications you made and in which files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This README is required so the GAP maintainers/others know what was changed; maintainers request notification of modifications and are particularly interested in bug fixes, improvements, and new functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and notification of published results using GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: If you publish mathematical results that were partly obtained using GAP, you should cite GAP and inform the GAP maintainers so they can add the publication to the GAP bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the requested citation format: '[GAP] The GAP Group, GAP - Groups, Algorithms, and Programming, Version 4.15.1; 2025 (https://www.gap-system.org)'. Inform support@gap-system.org about such publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bug report content and submission practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting bugs to support@gap-system.org, include a short, self-contained excerpt of a GAP session showing both input and output that illustrates the problem, a comment why you think it is a bug, and the machine/OS/compiler (if UNIX/Linux) and GAP version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide minimal reproducible examples and the execution environment to facilitate diagnosis; also send a brief message when you install GAP so maintainers can track usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help system invocation syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic help query form is ?[book :][?]topic, and the first question mark must be in the first position after the gap> prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search strings book and topic are normalized before searching (see normalization criterion). When multiple manual sections match, a numbered list of topics is shown and matches can be accessed with ?number. There are additional special commands starting with ? explained in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help search string normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a help search starts, the book and topic strings are normalized: backslashes and quotes removed; parentheses and braces replaced by blanks; non-ASCII treated as ISO-latin1 and accented letters replaced by non-accented counterparts; whitespace normalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This normalization makes searches case-insensitive and tolerant of various input forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help browsing commands and their semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The help system provides navigation commands: ?< and ?> to move to previous/next section/subsection, ?<< and ?>> to jump to chapter begins or next chapter, ?- and ?+ to navigate the history of displayed sections, ?books to list known books, and ?[book:]sections or ?[book:][chapters] to show tables of contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ?- and ?+ navigate history without altering it; ?& redisplays the last shown section, and with ?& the next preferred viewer is used. Some short commands have special behaviors described in Section 2.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help viewer configuration (SetHelpViewer) and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: SetHelpViewer(viewer1, viewer2, ...) sets a prioritized list of viewers; the first available viewer whose format matches the book is used. Calling with no arguments shows the current setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'screen' viewer (text pager) is always appended silently. Use SetUserPreference("HelpViewers", [...]) in gap.ini to change defaults. The order of arguments gives priority; ?& cycles to the next possible viewer in the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized help viewers and their limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual documents recognized viewers (e.g., 'screen', 'firefox', 'xpdf', 'acroread', 'links2', 'w3m', 'lynx', 'pdf viewer', 'less', 'more', macOS variants) and notes their platform-specific behaviors and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'screen' uses text Pager; 'xpdf' (X) can open pdf pages and be reused; 'acroread' cannot be given remote commands or start on a specific page so GAP prints page numbers instead; many pdf viewers cannot open at named destinations; 'Skim' (macOS) can open a PDF on a given page. Text-based HTML viewers may render formulae poorly for old books using symbol fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help display formats and tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Help books may be available in text, PDF, and HTML formats; each has advantages and limitations for readability and formula rendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text is default and best for terminal display (but complicated math may be hard to read); PDF is good for printing and often contains hyperlinks; HTML provides web browsing and cross-reference navigation but formulae may render poorly unless special fonts/technology are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal/pager recommendations for help text
rubrics_metrics.description: Text versions of manuals are formatted assuming at least 80 characters per line and a fixed-width font; UTF-8 terminals are suggested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminals in UTF-8 with fixed-width fonts work best; ISO-8859-X terminals also work reasonably. For paging, prefer external pagers (less or more) and configure PagerOptions; the internal builtin pager is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pager usage and argument forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Pager(lines) displays text page-by-page. The argument lines may be a single string, a list of strings, or a record with component lines and optional components 'formatted', 'start', and 'exitAtEnd'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: formatted=true avoids automatic line breaking; start can be an integer (first line) or a search string; exitAtEnd controls whether the pager exits automatically at end. Configure the 'Pager' user preference (e.g., 'less') and 'PagerOptions' for external pagers using SetUserPreference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command-line option syntax rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All GAP command-line options start with a hyphen followed by a single letter; options must not be grouped (e.g., 'gap -gq' is invalid); options that require an argument must have the argument separated by whitespace (e.g., 'gap -m 256m'). Boolean options toggle the current value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On UNIX GAP distinguishes upper- and lower-case options. During startup, a wrapper script may set defaults that differ from the manual. Current command line option values are available in GAPInfo.CommandLineOptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common command-line options and their semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual documents many options and their behaviors. Examples: -A toggles loading of suggested packages; -b toggles the startup banner; -c <gapcode> executes given GAP code; -D toggles short messages while reading files (debugging); -E disables readline usage; -e prevents quitting on Ctrl-D (do not use when input is file/pipe); -f enables line editing; -g prints garbage collection messages (-g twice increases verbosity); -h/--help prints option summary and exits; -K/--limitworkspace prevents attempting to allocate more memory and exits if limit hit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some options are for debugging, some for interactive behavior. Boolean toggles can be repeated to flip back. Examples and output formats are provided in the manual for interpreting messages (e.g., garbage collector messages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Package loading and OS/dependency considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some packages may be loaded automatically at GAP startup if present; packages that depend on external programs may only be available on operating systems where those programs exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should be aware that package availability can vary by OS and that LoadPackage must be called for packages marked '(not loaded)' in the help books until dependencies are available.
